text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Under the executive regulations for the law on commercial properties, leases can be inherited by only one generation and rents will go up 10 percent a year.
- The international conference on Islam and the West ends today with the message that Islam is not the enemy of the West and peaceful coexistence is the responsibility of all.

- President Hosni Mubarak endorsed the following military appointments: Major-General Galal Abbas Mohamed as head of the military training staff, Major-General Ali Maher Hegab as head of the operations staff, Major-General Hamdi Wahiba as commander of the Second Field Army and Major-General Mohamed Sabri Salaheddin as director of armoured forces.

- The executive of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) meets today in Washington for the second quarterly review of the Egyptian economy. IMF executive director Abdel Shakour Shaalan said the review would cover the government's 1997/8 budget, trade liberalisation and privatisation. Shaalan said the aims for the period up to September 1998 were to achieve growth of seven to eight percent, cut inflation and raise the investment rate to 25 from 18 percent of GDP.

- President Hosni Mubarak issued a presidential decree yesterday filling in the executive details of the law on renting non-residential property. Cabinet Affairs Minister Talaat Hammad said this cleared up all ambiguities.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid announced that it has been decided to sell 35 companies through the stock exchange between now and March next year. He said selling shares through the stock exchange was the best method of privatisation.
- Culture Minister Farouk Hosni said it has been decided to move the statue of Ramses II from Ramses Square in central Cairo to Mit Rahina (Memphis), where the statue came from.
- Mubarak will meet Israeli Labour Party leader Ehud Barak today. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa had talks with Barak yesterday evening on saving the peace process and implementing the peace agreements.
- Mubarak phoned King Fahd of Saudi Arabia on bilateral relations and regional and international developments.
- The head of a Chinese delegation said President Jiang Zemin had given instructions that every effort must be made to set up a free trade zone in Suez.
- After 16 years on the run, leading terrorist Hussein Ahmed Hussein has been arrested. Hussein was a member of the Jihad organisation accused of killing president Anwar Sadat.
